why_angle: The Club Car lineup page these shoppers land on lists only starting prices and speed, and the dealer inventory pages show no specs at all. None of them gives a pack's kWh, Club Car's own spec-sheet figure that a lithium Onward keeps 86–91% of its first-year range after four years against 25–38% for lead-acid, or a price per kWh for the 48V conversion kits. This page carries all three, each worked out from the maker's own sheet or store.
must: Pick the Club Car Onward 4 Passenger with XR lithium

page.title: Golf Cart with Lithium Battery: Which Keeps Its Range (2026)
page.h1: Golf cart with lithium battery: which one still has its range in year four
page.desc: Club Car's own figures: a lithium Onward keeps 86–91% of its range after four years, lead-acid 25–38%. New lithium carts and 48V conversion kits compared.
page.answer: Short answer. A golf cart with a lithium battery keeps its range: Club Car's official figures give the Onward lithium 7.0 kWh XR pack 30–50 miles after four years, against 5–15 miles for the lead-acid Onward. Pick the Club Car Onward 4 Passenger with XR lithium.

page.after:
What the differences mean

All Club Car range figures are the maker's estimates for non-lifted carts unless noted. The low end assumes maximum payload on moderate hills. The high end assumes only the driver, on flat ground.

  • Range kept after four years (Onward 4 Passenger). Lead-acid: 5 ÷ 20 = 25% at the low end and 15 ÷ 40 = 38% at the high end. HP lithium: 18 ÷ 20 = 90% and 30 ÷ 35 = 86%. XR lithium: 30 ÷ 35 = 86% and 50 ÷ 55 = 91%.
  • XR vs base pack. 7.0 ÷ 4.0 kWh = 1.75× the energy. After four years that means 30–50 mi against 18–30 mi.
  • Weight. Onward 4 XR: 1,070 − 794 = 276 lb lighter than lead-acid. Redodo kit: 383 − 82 = 301 lb less battery weight, by Redodo's figures.
  • Kit cost per kWh. Redodo: $1,149.99 ÷ 5.12 kWh = $225 per kWh. Vatrer: $1,579.99 ÷ 5.376 kWh = $294 per kWh.
  • Kit vs Club Car's base factory pack. Redodo: 5.12 ÷ 4.0 = 1.28, so 28% more energy. Vatrer: 5.376 ÷ 4.0 = 1.34, so 34% more. Club Car's XR pack (7.0 kWh) is still larger than either kit.
  • Kit vs a new cart. $1,149.99 ÷ $10,099 = 11.4%, and $1,579.99 ÷ $10,099 = 15.6%, of the lowest Onward starting MSRP.
  • Refill time. Redodo: 100 Ah ÷ 18 A = 5.6 h, which matches Redodo's stated time. Onward 2 Passenger: 4.0 kWh ÷ 0.65 kW ≈ 6.2 h on the base charger and 7.0 kWh ÷ 0.90 kW ≈ 7.8 h on the XR charger. These Club Car times are a lower limit worked out from the charger rating. Club Car itself says only that lithium charges up to 40% faster than lead-acid.

Why range after four years decides it

In its first year, a lead-acid Onward 4 Passenger is rated at 20–40 mi. That equals or beats the base 4.0 kWh lithium pack (20–35 mi). The difference shows up with age on Club Car's own spec sheet. By year four, lead-acid falls to 5–15 mi (5–10 mi lifted). The base lithium pack keeps 18–30 mi, and the 7.0 kWh XR pack keeps 30–50 mi. The Onward 2 Passenger shows the same pattern: lead-acid goes from 30–50 mi to 10–15 mi, and XR lithium from 45–60 mi to 40–55 mi. Lithium Onwards also get a 375 A controller instead of 250 A, a 4.7 hp (3.5 kW) rated motor instead of 3.3 hp (2.4 kW), and, on the Onward 2 Passenger, the 7-inch display and dual wireless chargers, which Club Car offers only with lithium.

The other factory option is E-Z-GO's ELiTE line. The Liberty ELiTE starts at $12,999 MSRP, and E-Z-GO's ELiTE page says personal carts include 8 years of battery coverage. Club Car's current pages give no battery warranty term; its 2019 lithium launch release said 6 years. E-Z-GO's spec pages give no pack kWh or range in miles, so the four-year comparison above can only be made for the Onward. The Liberty spec page lists 11.7 hp (8.7 kW) without saying whether that is a rated or a peak figure, so it can't be set against the Onward's 4.7 hp rated figure.

Converting a cart you already own. Both kits ship with a matched 58.4 V lithium charger, so don't reuse the old lead-acid charger. On a Club Car Precedent or a later DS, Club Car's service manual puts the On-Board Computer (OBC) in the charging circuit. ROYPOW, which sells conversion kits, says the OBC has to be bypassed with a jumper harness for lithium. Neither kit listing says whether a bypass harness is included, so ask the seller before ordering. The Redodo kit covers the most cart makes for the least money per kWh: {buy:redodo-48v-100ah-golf-cart-conversion-kit}. Vatrer's kit is listed specifically for 48 V Club Car DS, Precedent, Tempo and Onward carts, with its own bracket: {buy:vatrer-48v-105ah-club-car-golf-cart-battery-kit}.

Not recommended

A new Onward with flooded lead-acid batteries if you drive it every day. It falls under the same starting MSRP listing as the lithium Onward and matches lithium range in year one. But Club Car rates it at 5–15 mi after four years, against 18–30 mi for the base lithium pack, and it weighs 1,070 lb against 797 lb.
